title: Prompt-ingest microqueue with deterministic ASCII shortcut and kernel-hint propagation
creator: Ava Chen
description: Reduce per-request prefill overhead for short and ASCII-dominant prompts by adding a lightweight session-aware microqueue, a deterministic ASCII fastpath in the tokenizer, and propagation of kernel selection hints from the prefill stage to the runtime scheduler. This ticket implements the ingest-side changes: a small bounded microqueue to coalesce rapid single-token prefill bursts, a stateless ASCII detection/shortcut that avoids full unicode normalization where safe, and an annotation header that carries kernel/attention-mode hints to downstream decode scheduling. The goal is to reduce median prefill latency by ~20-35% on common chat workloads and reduce tokenization CPU usage at high QPS while preserving correctness for non-ASCII inputs.
acceptance_criteria: Median prefill latency reduction >= 20% on internal chat workload benchmark (ASCII-heavy)
99th percentile prefill latency not regressed by more than 5% for mixed/unicode prompts
No correctness regressions observed in tokenization unit tests and e2e conversation tests
Kernel hint header successfully received and consumed by decode scheduler in <= 1ms added overhead
Feature gated and toggleable per-customer via routing policy and config flags
technical_notes: Microqueue: bounded circular buffer per serving worker with 1-4 slot batching window and max wait 1-2ms to collect coalesced tasks

ASCII shortcut: fast validator that checks bytes for <= 0x7F and runs an ASCII-only tokenizer codepath that skips normalization and multi-byte decode; falls back to full tokenizer on any non-ASCII byte
Kernel-hint propagation: add lightweight header 'X-Runtime-Kernel-Hint' with values like 'fp16_lowlatency', 'int8_throughput', 'kv-prefetch' produced by prefix analysis heuristics
Safety: ASCII shortcut must be deterministic and produce identical token sequence as full tokenizer for ASCII inputs; add fuzz tests comparing outputs across corpus
Observability: emit metrics for microqueue occupancy, shortcut hit/miss ratio, fallback reasons, and hint acceptance by scheduler
Threading: microqueue processing stays on worker affinity to avoid cross-core contention; use lock-free operations where possible
Graceful degradation: config flag to disable fastpath per-customer or globally; fallback path always available
implementation_plan: 1) Prototype microqueue and ASCII fastpath in an internal worker branch; benchmark latencies with synthetic and recorded traffic
2) Add kernel-hint header emission from prefill stage after prompt analysis; design header schema and schema versioning
3) Integrate minimal consumer in decode scheduler that reads hint and logs acceptance metric; do not change scheduling behavior in first rollout
4) Add exhaustive unit and fuzz tests ensuring token sequence parity between fastpath and full tokenizer for ASCII inputs
5) Add telemetry counters and dashboards (Grafana) for occupancy, hit/miss, latency deltas
6) Canary rollout to 5% of traffic for non-critical customers, measure regressions and fallback rates
7) Iterate on microqueue thresholds (slots, wait time) based on tail-latency tradeoffs, then expand rollout
rollout_plan: Feature behind runtime feature-flag toggles; config per-deployment and per-customer
Canary stage 1: internal traffic only (10k reqs) for 48 hours
Canary stage 2: 5% of hosted API traffic mapped to low-risk orgs for 72 hours
Monitor: prefill median/P95/P99, tokenization CPU, microqueue occupancy and fallback reasons
Rollback: immediate global disable if P99 prefill latency increases > 10% or tokenization error rate > 0.01%
Post-rollback: automated incident runbook to capture heap/stack traces and microqueue state dump
metrics: tokenization_latency_ms p50/p95/p99 (segregated by ASCII-fastpath hits vs misses)
